title: Field diary: inference workshop — quick takeaways & micro experiments
content:
Context: attended internal 2-day inference workshop (informal run-through of kernel optimizations, rollout stories, and messy production trade-offs). This doc = scratch diary + things I want to try this sprint.

Day 1 (Nov 14) — morning fuzz: session on KV cache fragmentation and multi-tenant eviction patterns
- Main idea: small shards that are nearly-full create big context misses under heavy parallelism. Lots of microbench numbers but the story: eviction churn > CPU overhead on CPU-side routing.
- Notes to self: re-run the 'kv-shard' microbench with varied sequence-lengths (128/512/2048) and with our 2 config profiles: auto-batch=on vs pinned-batch=64.
- Quick hack idea: add a tiny LRU hysteresis window (5s) before marking a key as stale — possibly reduces churn for conversational workloads.

Day 1 afternoon — panel: routing fallbacks and rollout safety
- Interesting failure mode: canary rollback triggered by tail-latency spikes that were actually caused by background model warming (cache cold starts). Observability needs a metric: 'model-warmness' or kv-hit-rate per route over time.
- Action: propose an alert that correlates kv-hit-rate drop + CPU steal to avoid false-positive rollbacks. Jira RINF-732 was mentioned.

Day 2 (Nov 15) — experiments brainstorm
- Hypothesis A: For medium-length dialogs (avg 600 tokens), forced micro-batching (batch size 8) + ephemeral prefix-cache yields lower 99th latency than aggressive auto-batching because batching reduces per-request kernel overhead while ephemeral prefix avoids eviction thrash.
- Hypothesis B: Quantize smaller FFN layers to int8 and keep attention kernels fp16 for price/quality sweet spot on A100-like hardware. Worth A/Bing on dedicated capacity.

Papers / links I skimmed (quick take):
- paper: "Sparse Key-Value Cache for Long Contexts" (arXiv link above). Good conceptual framing about shard placement.
- blog: internal post on "rollouts that don't roll back on warmup" — need clearer example traces to use in playbook.
- PR: runtime#842 — contains a small kernel-chooser refactor; seems safe to copy parts into a local branch for testing.

Pocket experiments (quick, low-friction) — priority order:
1) kv-lru-hysteresis: instrumented microbench (2 hours) + perf dashboard patch (Omar to review). Expected outcome: reduce eviction rate by ~15% on conversational trace.
2) batch-vs-ephemeral: synthetic replay of 10k conversational requests with controlled sequence-length distribution. Use dedicated small pool to avoid noisy neighbor variance. Goal: measure p50/p95/p99 and cost tokens/sec.
3) mixed-quant-sensitivity: run eval on 100 prompts from our baseline eval set — check degradation on completion quality (BLEU-like / ranking) after int8 FFN vs fp16 baseline.

Operational notes / heuristics to capture in playbook draft:
- Metric to add: kv-hit-rate-by-route, model-warmness (fraction of requests with zero kv-hits in last N seconds), kernel-switch-count-per-minute.
- Canary recipe: pause automatic rollback for 120s if model-warmness < 0.2 (i.e., warmup in-progress).

Open questions / TODOs to discuss with Lina:
- How conservative should the hysteresis be? 5s feels right for chat, but for web search flows might be too long. Need traffic-class config.
- Can we add a lightweight synthetic-warmup request during model switch to pre-fill hot keys? Risk: extra cost, but may reduce rollback noise.

Random observations (notes to self):
- Speaker referred to "prefix-affinity" — reminds me of our prefix caching experiments in May 2027; revisit logs from that run (search for "prefix-affinity" tag in internal S3).
- People really like clear rollback telemetries. Ops story sells better than kernel optimization when talking to product.

Immediate next steps (within 1 week):
- Create branch: maya/kv-hysteresis, push microbench harness, open draft PR (target runtime#842 baseline).
- Put together reproducible batch-vs-ephemeral replay (script + small sample trace).
- Sync with Lina on canary playbook, add two new observability panels: kv-hit-rate/time and model-warmness.

Notes-to-self final: keep notes terse here. This doc will become the basis for a short internal walkthrough (10-12 slides) for infra sync. If things look promising, escalate to eng-leads for Dedicated run and potential eval on customer workload.

-- end --
